title: FastAPI in Containers — Docker
note: Build from scratch on the official Python image; the tiangolo/uvicorn-gunicorn-fastapi base image is deprecated ('You should probably not use this base image'). uv projects: export the lock with 'uv export --format requirements-txt --no-dev --no-emit-project --output-file requirements.txt'. Always use the exec form of CMD so shutdown is graceful and lifespan events fire (shell form costs ~10 s on recreate/stop). Copy requirements.txt before source to preserve the Docker cache layer. One process per container when a cluster handles replication; --workers N only for the simple single-server case. --proxy-headers behind a TLS-terminating proxy. Multi-worker/multi-replica is a reminder that our API must stay stateless w.r.t. coordination.

title: PixiJS 8 — Ticker
note: Ticker 'provides a powerful and flexible mechanism for executing callbacks on every animation frame' for game loops, animations and 'any time-based updates'; can be constructed standalone (new Ticker(); add(fn, ctx); addOnce; remove; start/stop; autoStart). Listener priority: higher runs earlier, UPDATE_PRIORITY.HIGH=50 / NORMAL=0 / LOW=-50. Frame clamping: minFPS 'Caps how slow frames are allowed to be. Used to clamp deltaTime'; maxFPS 'Limits how fast the ticker runs'; maxFPS=0 for unlimited. Basis for owning the render loop in a dedicated Ticker outside React reconciliation, and for treating deltaTime as display-only (simulation time must come from telemetry, per our clock-domain rule).

title: Playwright — Assertions
note: Auto-retrying locator assertions 'will retry until the assertion passes, or the assertion timeout is reached'; default assertion timeout 5 s, configurable via testConfig.expect. Warns that non-retrying assertions on asynchronously-loaded pages 'can lead to a flaky test' and to prefer auto-retrying assertions, expect.poll or expect.toPass. Documents expect.soft + expect(test.info()).errors, expect.configure({ timeout }), and the custom expect message argument. Basis for our readiness strategy.

title: Playwright — Navigations
note: 'There is no way to tell that the page is loaded, it depends on the page, framework, etc.' Playwright auto-waits for actionability; recommends explicit page.waitForURL for navigations; warns about poor hydration.

title: Playwright — Network
note: Source for the deterministic alternative to idle-waiting: page.route / browserContext.route with route.fulfill to stub telemetry, page.waitForResponse(glob|regexp|predicate) to await a specific response, page.on('request'/'response') for event-level assertions, and the note to set serviceWorkers: 'block' if route-based mocking appears to miss events.

title: Playwright — Page API (page.goto, page.waitForLoadState)

This is the primary citation for banning networkidle as a readiness signal in our continuous-telemetry cockpit.

title: uv — Using workspaces
note: Workspace = 'a collection of one or more packages, called workspace members, that are managed together'; single shared lockfile; 'uv lock operates on the entire workspace at once, while uv run and uv sync operate on the workspace root by default, though both accept a --package argument'. [tool.uv.workspace] with required members / optional exclude globs; root is also a member; cross-member deps via { workspace = true } and are editable; a member's own tool.uv.sources entry overrides the root even when its marker does not match the platform. Limits: single requires-python across the workspace (intersection); not suited to members needing separate venvs (use path deps); and crucially 'uv can't ensure that packages don't import dependencies declared by another workspace member' — citable justification for our own import/authority-boundary tests.

title: Pathfinding Benchmarks: File Formats (.map and .scen specification)
publisher: Moving AI Lab, University of Alberta
note: Authoritative format grammar. .map header: 'type octile', 'height y', 'width x', 'map'; ASCII grid, (0,0) upper-left; characters . G @ O T S W with the stated passability. .scen: begins 'version x.x' (1.0); each line has 9 whitespace fields: Bucket, map, width, height, start_x, start_y, goal_x, goal_y, optimal_length; optimal length assumes sqrt(2) diagonals and no corner cutting through walls. There is NO field for service time, task release time, load, or task identity — proof that MAPF scenarios are not pickup-delivery workloads.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods — Bootstrap Plot
note: Defines the bootstrap procedure (subsample with replacement, typically 500-1000 resamples) and the percentile interval by ordering resampled statistics and reading off percentiles; states the motivation ('many situations in which the uncertainty formulas are mathematically intractable. The bootstrap provides a method for calculating the uncertainty in these cases'); and cautions the bootstrap is not appropriate for all distributions/statistics.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods — Confidence Limits for the Mean
note: States that confidence intervals for other location estimators such as the median are 'mathematically difficult or intractable' and that these cases use the bootstrap. Also clarifies that a 95% interval does not mean a 95% probability for a given sample — the level is attached to the method. Used to justify reporting the paired-ratio interval as a 95% NOMINAL interval.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods — Measures of Location
note: Source for Tukey/Mosteller's robustness of validity vs robustness of efficiency, and for the statements that a mean-based interval 'lacks robustness of validity' for non-normal data while the median 'tends to have robustness of validity but not robustness of efficiency'. Basis for recommending median-of-ratios + percentile interval over mean-of-ratios at small n.

title: Nav2 — Collision Monitor Node
note: Explicit non-certification statement: 'this node is done at the CPU level with any form of sensor. As such, this does not provide hard real-time safety certifications'. Four models: Stop, Slowdown, Limit, Approach; most aggressive wins (stop > slow 50% > slow 10%). Zone shapes: polygon, footprint, circle, VelocityPolygon (velocity-dependent). Sources: LaserScan, PointCloud2, Range, Costmap. Exclusion zones mask a source's own returns and are fail-safe ('if the zone transform is unavailable, no points are removed, so collision protection is never silently lost'). source_timeout default 2.0 s stops the robot when data goes stale; stop_pub_timeout default 1.0 s; use_realtime_priority default false requires rtprio 99 in /etc/security/limits.conf. NOTE: rolling docs, not Jazzy — parameter names must be re-verified against Jazzy.

title: ROS on DDS
publisher: Open Source Robotics Foundation (design.ros2.org); W. Woodall; written 2014-06, last modified 2019-07
note: Rationale only — the article self-declares it predates final decisions. Key points: DDS is OMG-standardised so behaviour is documented and auditable; 'The default discovery system provided by DDS... is distributed... without the need for a tool like the ROS master', which removes a single point of failure; QoS spans best-effort to reliable, suiting lossy wireless. Honest caveats quoted: adopting DDS adopts that middleware's culture; the standard body is 'slow moving'; 'it isn't the feeling of a large community to fall back on with DDS'. Licensed CC BY 3.0 per its footer.

title: ROS 2 — Quality of Service settings
note: Fetched as raw RST. Policies: history, depth, reliability, durability, deadline, lifespan, liveliness, lease duration. Compatibility is request-vs-offered: best-effort publisher + reliable subscription is incompatible ('No'); volatile publisher + transient-local subscription gives 'No communication'. Incompatibility is silent: 'When connections are not made, no messages will be passed between the publisher and subscription.' Detection requires QoS events (offered/requested incompatible QoS, deadline missed, liveliness lost/changed) and matched events. Default pub/sub = keep-last depth 10, reliable, volatile, system-default liveliness. 'even the reliable policy in ROS 2 is implemented using UDP.'
